record.original_question: Let T be a rooted labelled tree with n parking spaces and let f be an n-mapping on [n]. For m drivers, write S(T, m) for the number of parking sequences that successfully park on T and S(f, m) for the analogous number for f. Is there a simple general characterization of the counting functions S(T, m) and S(f, m), rather than only case-by-case formulas or bounds?

evidence.quote: (1) Given a tree T or a mapping f, is it possible in general to give some simple characterization of the numbers S(T, m) and S(f, m), respectively?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T$ be a rooted labelled tree on the vertex set $[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, regarded as a parking structure: each vertex is a parking space, and each non-root edge is oriented toward the root, giving each non-root vertex a unique outgoing edge. A sequence of $m\le n$ drivers arrives one by one; driver $j$ has a preferred space $s_j\in[n]$ and proceeds as follows: starting at vertex $s_j$, the driver parks there if it is unoccupied; otherwise the driver follows the directed edges toward the root, parking at the first unoccupied vertex encountered. If the driver reaches the root and it is occupied, the driver fails. The sequence $(s_1,\dots,s_m)\in[n]^m$ is called a parking sequence for $T$ with $m$ drivers if all $m$ drivers successfully park. Let
$$S(T,m)=\#\{(s_1,\dots,s_m)\in[n]^m:\text{all }m\text{ drivers park on }T\}.$$

Analogously, let $f:[n]\to[n]$ be a mapping (an $n$-mapping), with functional digraph having an edge from $i$ to $f(i)$ for each $i$. A driver with preference $s\in[n]$ starts at $s$ and follows the directed edges $i\mapsto f(i)$, parking at the first unoccupied vertex; if the driver returns to a previously visited (occupied) vertex without finding a free space, the driver fails. Define $S(f,m)$ as the number of sequences in $[n]^m$ for which all $m$ drivers successfully park.

Problem: Give a simple, general structural characterization of the counting functions $S(T,m)$ (for arbitrary rooted labelled trees $T$) and $S(f,m)$ (for arbitrary $n$-mappings $f$), beyond case-by-case formulas, bounds, or treatments of extremal cases.
artifact.category_tag: Parking functions on trees and mappings
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent survey of parking problems on random trees. Existing literature (Kenyon–Yin, Panholzer and collaborators, Yan et al.) provides characterizations and bounds in extremal or specific cases, but no general simple characterization of $S(T,m)$ or $S(f,m)$ for arbitrary trees and mappings appears in the literature as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Short survey of results and open problems for parking problems on random trees
status_evidence.snippet: Given a tree T or a mapping f, is it possible in general to give some simple characterization of the numbers S(T, m) and S(f, m), respectively?
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as an open question in a 2025 survey.

status_evidence.title: Parking functions for trees and mappings
status_evidence.snippet: We study parking functions on rooted labelled trees and on the functional digraphs of mappings, establishing bounds and characterizations in extremal cases.
status_evidence.claim: Existing characterizations are only for extremal cases or specific tree families, not general.
